value.subtitle: Departure boards, status rules and train composition for stations — an interface read at thirty metres, in a hurry, usually by someone who is already late.

hero.alt: Travellers reading departure and arrival boards in a station concourse
hero.caption: The real reading conditions: distance, crowd, glare, hurry.

sections.heading: The brief was the station, not the screen
sections.body: The programme started as three commitments. Nothing about pixels. But the departure board is where those promises are kept or broken: it has roughly four seconds to say whether the train exists, when it leaves and where to stand.

facts.title: Open market
facts.body: Adapt to a rail market opening to competition.

facts.title: Accessible
facts.body: Be more accessible, to every traveller.

facts.title: Every situation
facts.body: Support travellers whatever is happening on the platform.

images.alt: Programme framing slides: adapt, support, be accessible
images.caption: Three commitments that all land on the same screen.

sections.heading: A palette built for distance
sections.body: These screens hang above a concourse: glare, oblique viewing angles, people reading while walking. The scale runs from blue-900 down to blue-50, with a single cyan accent held in reserve for live information — anything that moves, updates or is about to happen. Because the accent is rare, it carries meaning instead of decoration.

images.alt: Colour scale from blue-900 to blue-50 with a cyan live accent
images.caption: One ramp, one accent, reserved for what is live.

sections.heading: Status is the whole design
sections.body: A row is never just a destination and a time. It is on time, approaching, delayed, cancelled or replaced by a coach — and each state has to survive glare, colour blindness and a glance from across the hall. So state is carried three times over: a mark, a colour and a word. A cancellation breaks the row’s entire promise, so the destination is struck through and the platform slot is emptied rather than left showing a number nobody should walk to.

images.alt: Departure and arrival rows carrying status marks
images.caption: Departures in blue, arrivals in green — same status vocabulary.

sections.heading: Which carriage, and where to stand
sections.body: Composition strips map the train onto the platform: numbered carriages, occupancy, the train number repeated so it can be matched with the board overhead. It is the piece that turns “the train is here” into “walk that way” — the difference between information and help.

images.alt: Train composition strips with numbered carriages and occupancy
images.caption: Composition and occupancy, in both reading contexts.

value.outro: The departures board on the home page is a live rebuild of this work, running in your browser — statuses, split-flap and clock included.
